recipes.title: How To Reverse Sear A Steak

ingredients.name: thick-cut steaks (ribeye, NY strip, or filet mignon, at least 1.5 to 2 inches thick)
high smoke-point oil (canola, avocado, or grapeseed oil)

steps: Pat the steaks completely dry with paper towels, then season generously on all sides with kosher salt and cracked black pepper.
Set a wire rack inside a rimmed baking sheet and arrange steaks on top of the rack.

Bake in the preheated oven for 25 to 45 minutes, monitoring with an instant-read probe thermometer until target internal pull temperature is reached (110°F for rare, 120°F for medium-rare, 130°F for medium).
Heat high smoke-point cooking oil in a heavy cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking.
Transfer steaks to the hot skillet and sear for 1 minute on the first side.
Flip the steaks, immediately drop the butter, smashed garlic cloves, and herb sprigs into the pan.
Tilt the skillet and rapidly spoon the foaming herb butter over the tops of the steaks for 1 minute until a crisp, deep mahogany crust forms.
Sear the fat caps and edges with tongs for 30 seconds, then transfer steaks to a warm board to rest for 5 to 7 minutes before slicing.
recipes.swaps: Applicable to bone-in or boneless cuts; beef tallow can replace butter for high-heat basting.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Rimmed baking sheet, wire roasting rack, cast iron skillet, instant-read probe thermometer. Ideal for cuts 1.5 inches thick or greater.
